So if you have a list of items, each item would be on a separate line. 3. **Example**: - Normal JSON: `{ "name": "Alice", "age": 30 }` - JSONL: `{"name":"Alice","age":30}\n{"name":"Bob","age":25}` 4. **Use in Evaluation Cases**: When you're writing evaluation cases, like for testing software, JSONL can be very useful because it makes each test case easy to read and manage. Each line is a separate test case, so you can quickly look through them or add new ones without confusion.
